title: Partners prepare to procure next batch of equipment for Polish plant
html:
Three Westinghouse AP1000 reactors are planned for the plant at the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site in the Choczewo municipality in Pomerania in northern Poland. The AP1000 reactor design uses modular construction techniques, enabling large structural modules to be built at factories and then installed at the site. The reactor building and systems consist of dozens of prefabricated, steel-concrete structural and mechanical modules.

In October, Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe (PEJ) gave Westinghouse the go-ahead to start ordering long-lead items (LLIs) for the project's first AP1000 unit. It said the scope of the order for the first unit covers six key components of the nuclear island, including the reactor containment vessel and associated structural modules.

Westinghouse subsequently placed conditional purchase orders with Polish companies Energomontaż-Północ Gdynia SA (EPG), FAMAK SA, Mostostal Kielce SA and Mostostal Krakow SA to support the first AP1000 unit at the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site. The conditional purchase orders cover the CA02 Walls Module Scope for Mostostal Kielce, the CA03 Module Scope for EPG, the CA05 Walls Module Scope for Mostostal Krakow, and the CA20 Floors Module Scope for FAMAK. Earlier this month, Japanese engineering firm IHI Corporation received an order from Westinghouse covering engineering and procurement activities for long-lead items for one containment vessel and an associated large steel module for the first unit.

Under the new letter of intent - signed during the 7th Ministerial Meeting of the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC) in Warsaw - PEJ and the Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium have now agreed to work on a mechanism for extending the scopes of contracts critical to the project schedule. In addition, the US partners will support PEJ in its negotiations with export credit agencies regarding financing for the investment project related to the supply of power plant components.

"Signing of the letter of intent marks the next stage in the process of ordering long-lead items for Poland's first nuclear power plant," PEJ said. It added: "Starting the procurement process for the next batch of LLIs early will help mitigate scheduling risks and ensure that the power plant is commissioned on schedule."

"The construction of Poland's first nuclear power plant is a strategic project that will strengthen our country's energy security and provide us with a stable source of energy for decades to come," said Miłosz Motyka, Minister of Energy. "At the same time, this project requires close cooperation with technology vendors and proper preparation of the subsequent phases of the investment project. We are pleased that Polish companies are playing an increasingly important role in this process. The letter of intent provides the basis for further discussions regarding the project's key components. This is crucial for both smooth progress of the power plant's construction and its schedule."

"From the very beginning, we have been consistently creating the conditions for the broadest possible participation of Polish companies in the nuclear power plant project," added Marek Woszczyk, President of the Management Board of PEJ. "Activities related to preparing contracts for key equipment represent the next step, which – while ensuring that the project remains on schedule – also enables Polish companies to participate not only in our project but also in the global supply chain for the modern nuclear energy sector."

Dan Lipman, President of Westinghouse's Global Business Initiatives, said: "By moving ahead with this group of long-lead items for the Lubiatowo-Kopalino project, PEJ has taken a key step in maintaining its schedule. It further strengthens our supply chain relationships, which will benefit both this AP1000 project and Polish industry."

Workforce development

Bechtel, Gdańsk University of Technology, and the University of South Carolina, through its Molinaroli College of Engineering and Computing, signed a memorandum of cooperation during PTEC 2026, opening a new chapter in cooperation between the academic communities of Poland and the USA in the field of nuclear energy.

The agreement builds on Bechtel's existing partnership with the University of South Carolina's Molinaroli College of Engineering and Computing, announced in October 2026, which established the Bechtel Nuclear Energy Workforce Development Fund to support nuclear education and workforce development. It also builds on Bechtel's cooperation with Polish universities since 2024 including Gdańsk University of Technology, bringing together relationships Bechtel has developed with leading academic institutions in both countries.

Through the memorandum of cooperation signed at PTEC, the parties will work together to identify areas where combining academic expertise from Poland and the USA with Bechtel's global industry experience can strengthen education and support the workforce needs of the growing nuclear energy industry in both countries.

PTEC 2026 is one of the key events dedicated to energy cooperation between the USA and Central and Eastern Europe, bringing together government representatives, leading energy companies, and institutions involved in the development of strategic infrastructure.

US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and Polish Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka released the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC) 2026 Chair Statement at the conclusion of the seventh P-TEC Ministerial and Business Forum in Warsaw. In the partnership, amongst other things, the countries: recognize civil nuclear energy as essential to reliable power generation and long-term energy security, and support advancement of current and next-generation technologies, consistent with national priorities; encourage investment in secure nuclear fuel supplies, workforce development, industrial capacity, and regulatory coordination to enable civil nuclear deployment at scale; and recognise the important contribution of firm, dispatchable generation, including coal, natural gas, and nuclear energy, to electricity affordability, grid reliability, and energy security, consistent with national priorities.

The background

In November 2022, the then Polish government selected Westinghouse AP1000 reactor technology for construction at the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site in the Choczewo municipality in Pomerania in northern Poland. In September 2023, Westinghouse, Bechtel and PEJ - a special-purpose vehicle 100% owned by Poland's State Treasury - signed an 18-month engineering services contract under which Westinghouse and Bechtel will finalise a site-specific design for a plant featuring three AP1000 reactors. In April last year, PEJ and the Westinghouse-Bechtel Consortium agreed the terms and conditions of an Engineering Development Agreement (EDA) after the previous agreement expired.

On 29 December 2025, PEJ announced it had signed an amendment to the Engineering Development Agreement with the Westinghouse-Bechtel Consortium. The amended scope of the agreement provides for the continuation of design works covering the nuclear island, turbine island, and the balance of plant, as well as further in-depth geological survey campaigns. This, it said, allows it to maintain the project schedule by advancing the power plant design and continuing field works, while simultaneously conducting negotiations and finalising the Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contract, "which will ultimately determine our cooperation with the Westinghouse-Bechtel Consortium".

In September, the Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium and PEJ announced they had agreed the main commercial and legal terms of the EPC contract, and plan to complete the contract negotiation process by the end of this year.
